jobs.desc:
The Preconstruction Estimating Department Administrative Specialist provides administrative, document control, and bid coordination support to Enterprise Electrical’s Preconstruction and Estimating team. This role organizes project information, tracks pursuit deadlines and submission requirements, coordinates vendor and subcontractor communications, and prepares proposal materials so estimators can develop accurate bids using current and complete information. The position supports the process from receipt of a bid invitation through proposal submission, bid follow-up, and transfer of awarded-project records.

Working under the direction of the Preconstruction Director or Chief Estimator, this position manages multiple administrative assignments with attention to accuracy, confidentiality, and follow-through. The Administrative Specialist anticipates missing information, communicates deadline risks, and adapts quickly as priorities change in a growing electrical construction business. Estimators retain responsibility for technical scope, quantities, labor assumptions, pricing decisions, and final estimate approval.

**Essential Functions, Duties, and Responsibilities**

Tasks may include, but are not limited to the following:

* Maintain the bid calendar, recording due dates, pre-bid meetings, site visits, review milestones, and customer submission requirements.

* Create project folders and maintain consistent naming, file organization, permissions, and document version control.

* Download, organize, and distribute drawings, specifications, addenda, bid forms, and customer instructions to the appropriate team members.

* Track document revisions and notify estimators of new addenda, changed deadlines, or updated submission requirements.

* Prepare and distribute invitations to bid using scope information and recipient lists approved by estimators.

* Maintain vendor and subcontractor contact information, bid lists, quotation logs, and records of follow-up activity.

Wilson Construction Company is a premier utility contractor specializing in complex electrical transmission and distribution line construction across the United States. * **General Administration & Liaison Support:** Manage reception and front desk duties (visitors, phones, mail, supplies), coordinate bid documents and job setup

Ripple Roofing & Construction is a fast-growing, owner-operated, Veteran-Owned contractor headquartered in Round Rock, TX. **What You’ll Do**

* **Own your pipeline:** Generate, close, and manage deals through our CRM.
* **Manage insurance restoration projects:** Perform inspections, meet adjusters, scope damage, write estimates, and secure signed contracts.
* **Collaborate with production:** Ensure smooth project hand-offs and deliver five-star customer experiences.

**Transparent & Duplicateable Pay Structure**

We eliminate confusing 10/50/50 split models so top producers control their own margin and max out their earning potential.

* **Direct Sales (15% Flat House Fee / 90% Net Profit):** You manage the project end-to-end. The company retains a flat **15% fee** on gross revenue. After direct job costs (materials and labor), you earn **90% of the net profit**.
* *Example:* On a **$20,000** job, Ripple retains **$3,000** (15%). If direct costs are $11,000, the profit pool is $6,000. **You pocket $5,400 (90%).**
* **Team Building & Mentorship (10% Recruiter Override):** Recruit and mentor reps to build a recurring passive income stream. You receive **10% of the net profit** earned on every job closed by reps you recruit.
* *Example:* When a rep you recruited nets a $6,000 profit pool on a project, **you earn a $600 passive override** for mentoring them.

**Compensation & Support**

* **Average 1st-Year OTE:** $150,000 – $200,000+ (top producer

**Position Summary**

Aquality Construction is seeking an organized, communicative, and proactive Project Coordinator (PC) to be the primary client-facing coordinator who guides customers through the company's full process — from initial sales contact through design, pre-construction, build, and a clean handover to Maintenance.

The PC is the conduit for coordination, clarity, and follow-up — not the technical decision-maker. Sales, the Designer, the Construction Manager, and Superintendents each own and approve the technical, financial, and schedule decisions within their phase; the PC keeps the project, the client, and every department on the same page and moving forward.

**Core Responsibilities**

**1. Client Communication Concierge**

* Serve as the consistent point of contact for client questions and updates across Sales, Design, and Construction.
* Provide quick, accurate responses; document critical decisions in writing when needed.
* Triage inbound requests and route them to the correct internal owner — Sales, Designer, Construction Manager, or Superintendent.
* Reduce client confusion by summarizing decisions, next steps, and owners after key touchpoints.

**2. Process Enforcement and Handoff Discipline**

* Keep projects aligned to the company's roadmap and phase gates; prevent skipped steps.
* Track what phase each project is in and what prerequisites must be complete before it advances.
* Push internal teams to follow the plan — professionally and persistently.

**3. Task and Follow-Up Management (Open-Loop Ownership)**

jobs.title: Billing Specialist
jobs.desc:
**About Professional Diversified Flooring, Inc.**

Professional Diversified Flooring was established in 1981 and is a leading provider of commercial flooring solutions. With a workforce exceeding 70 office employees and over 400 field labor, the company specializes in comprehensive flooring services for commercial spaces throughout Los Angeles, Orange County, San Diego, Las Vegas, Phoenix, and surrounding areas. Leveraging proprietary technology and a distinctive project management methodology, Professional Diversified Flooring ensures meticulous attention to detail in every undertaking. Our portfolio encompasses a wide range of projects, from corporate offices to casinos and from healthcare to hospitality, positioning us not merely as flooring specialists, but as strategic partners in design and construction adding maximum value to our clients and their clients.

**THE ROLE**
------------

Billing at PDF does two things: it bills, and it collects. The Billing Specialist owns both, end to end, for the projects assigned to them — from verifying the contract, through progress billing, pay applications, portal submission, lien releases and retention, to collecting the money and closing the job.

Roughly 60% of your time is billing, 30% is collecting, and 10% is the compliance paperwork that gates payment in construction. You are the customer-facing voice of our accounting department to General Contractor project accountants and End User AP teams, and the person our Project Managers rely on to turn finished work into cash.

This is not a data-entry job. The volume is real — a proficient specialist produces 150–200 billings and around $3 million a month — but the work is judgment: reading a subcontract's billing terms, knowing how much can reasonably be billed on a job, catching an over-billing before the GC does, and knowing how far to push a collection before escalating.

You will report to our Billing Manager and work alongside a small, tight team in our Irvine office

jobs.title: Field Runner/Full-Time Job Coordinator
jobs.desc:
This is a starting role with a real future. You start as our runner. If you're good, you grow into our full-time Job Coordinator, the person who keeps every job on track.

Read this first. We need someone organized, reliable and trustworthy. If you lose track of things, run late, or don't answer your phone, this isn't for you.

If people describe you as the one who always has it handled, keep reading.

What we do: High-end kitchen and bath remodels in South Jersey. We're growing fast, and we promote from within.

**Your path with us:**

* Weeks 1–2: Runner (paid part-time trial). Learn our crews, our jobs and how we work. It's a chance for both of us to see if it's a fit.
* After 2 weeks: Full-time. If it's working, you go full-time.
* Next: Full-Time Job Coordinator. You run the day-to-day across multiple jobs: scheduling crews, managing materials, keeping clients updated, and making sure every job starts and finishes on time. More responsibility, more pay.

**What you'll do as a runner:**

* Start each day at the shop and meet our crews.
* Get everything set up so crews can start on time.
* Pick up and drop off materials between the shop, suppliers and jobsites.
* Be a friendly, professional face for our clients on site.
* Log notes, deliveries and job updates clearly and on time.
* Be on call when a job needs something fast.

**You're a fit if you:**

* Have a reliable car, a valid license and a clean driving record.
* Are highly organized and detail-oriented.
* Communicate clearly with customers and crews.
* Are comfortable using your phone to log notes and updates.
* Answer calls and show up when you say you will.
* Want to grow into a leadership role, not just clock in.

**Pay:** $18–$28/hr based on experience, with raises as you move up.

**To apply: text (856) 295 - 2284 with:**

* Your name.
* What car you drive.
* One sentence on why people can count on you.
* We only respond to applicants who answer all 3.

The expert 3D CAD Records & Data Analyst serves as a key liaison between the Records team, Engineering groups, and program leadership within Gas Transmission Engineering and Design. The Analyst will coordinate SAP tasks related to drawing custody and work order management, maintain and enhance reporting dashboards, and support cross-functional collaboration between engineering, drafting, construction, and records teams. * Maintain accurate estimating records, historical costs, and project documentation.
* Support project scheduling, construction phasing, and procurement planning.
* Assist with transitioning projects from preconstruction to operations.

* Maintain an accessible record of schedule revisions and commitments; flag incomplete information instead of treating assumptions as confirmed.

* Use Aspire scheduling and work-order data as a planning tool, keeping it current and accurate so it supports schedule decisions rather than serving only as a record.

**About Us**  
Restoration 1 of Huntington Beach is a licensed disaster restoration and environmental remediation company (CA GC #1131316) serving Orange County. We handle water, fire, and mold mitigation and reconstruction, working directly with homeowners, insurance carriers, and adjusters. We're growing and need a sharp estimator who can write accurate, defensible Xactimate estimates that get approved and paid.

You'll own the estimating process from first inspection to final approval. That means scoping losses on site, building detailed Xactimate estimates for both mitigation and reconstruction, and working with adjusters to get every legitimate line item paid.

* Review completed job files so final invoices match the work performed
* Coordinate with the field crew and office on scope, materials, and job progress
* Track estimate status, approvals, and receivables

**Requirements**

* 2+ years writing Xactimate estimates in insurance restoration (required)
* Strong knowledge of Xactimate line items, pricing, sketch, and estimate structure
* Understanding of the water mitigation process and IICRC S500/S520 standards
* Proven experience writing supplements and negotiating with adjusters
* Strong construction knowledge: drywall, flooring, cabinets, paint, trim, and so on
* Detail-oriented, organized, and able to manage multiple files at once
* Valid California driver's license

**Job Summary**

The Project Scheduler supports the planning, coordination, and monitoring of construction schedules across multiple projects. This role primarily focuses on assisting with schedule development during the proposal phase and partnering with superintendents and project teams to maintain, update, and improve active project schedules. The Project Scheduler plays a key role in ensuring schedules are realistic, properly maintained, and aligned with project goals and field conditions.

*Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

* Analyze drawings, specifications, and bid documents to identify scheduling constraints, risks, and sequencing considerations.
* Review and evaluate project schedules created by superintendents and project managers for logic, duration accuracy, and completeness.
* Collaborate with superintendents and project managers to update and maintain active project schedules, ensuring alignment with field progress and conditions.
* Identify potential schedule conflicts, delays, or impacts and assist project teams in developing mitigation or recovery plans.
* Facilitate and participate in regular schedule review meetings with project teams.
* Track and monitor key project milestones and schedule performance across multiple projects.
* Assist project team to prepare and distribute internal and client-facing schedule updates and reports.
* Provide guidance, direction, and support to field teams on scheduling best practices and use of scheduling tools, especially with regard to difficult project impacts. Assess the impact of design changes and schedule slippages.
* Assist in standardizing scheduling processes, templates, and reporting methods across projects.

Position Summary

The AP & AR Specialist is responsible for ensuring that the accounting system accurately and promptly reflects what the company owes and what it has earned. The position owns accounts payable and the assigned accounts receivable functions. It ensures expenses are properly coded, documented, reconciled, and paid on time, and that completed work and approved changes become timely, accurate customer billings.

The role directly impacts cash flow, cash-flow planning, job-cost accuracy, month-end reporting, vendor relationships, and the company’s ability to understand true project profitability. Unentered invoices understate expenses and liabilities, can make profitability appear stronger than it is, and leave management with an incomplete view of upcoming cash needs; delayed billings and unrecorded receipts hold back or obscure cash the company has already earned. The objective is not speed alone, but accurate, efficient, and consistent processing that keeps the books as close to real time as practical. The first six months of employment are a training period, after which the employee is expected to perform both AP and AR functions with minimal oversight.

* Process vendor invoices promptly and accurately, entering the correct vendor, amount, invoice date, GL account, job, cost class, phase, task, and tax coding.
* Maintain a steady daily processing pace throughout the week so invoices do not build into week-end or month-end backlogs.
* Work with Project Managers and Foremen to obtain missing job, phase, task, PO, approval, or supporting information.
* Scan and match invoices, packing slips, and POs; enter approved invoices into Foundation with support attached and maintain organized electronic records.

**About Us**

Excel Restoration is a leading restoration and disaster-recovery company specializing in water mitigation, fire damage restoration, mold remediation, and full reconstruction. We’ve built a strong reputation on quality work, fast response, and taking care of people on what is often one of the worst days of their lives. Most of our work comes through warm referrals from partners who already trust us — so speed, communication, and execution matter.

**Position Overview**

As a Dispatch Manager, you are the person responsible for making sure the right people get to the right job at the right time — and that our customers never feel like they’ve been forgotten.

You’ll lead our dispatch operation, supporting and holding our dispatchers accountable while coordinating crews, Project Managers, and resources across a constantly changing schedule. Your job is to keep all of those moving pieces organized and make smart decisions quickly.

This is a leadership role, but it is not a desk-only management position. You’ll be actively involved in the day-to-day operation of Dispatch, helping your team solve problems, making scheduling decisions, communicating with Operations and Project Management, and stepping in when something needs to be escalated.

* Lead and manage the day-to-day Dispatch operation, ensuring our team is responsive, organized, and accountable.

headlined_rolled.title: Construction Sourcing Manager, Principal
headlined_rolled.desc:
**ABOUT THE ROLE**

Skilled trade labor is one of the hardest things to secure on a data center build. This Sourcing Manager owns how Hut 8 finds, qualifies, and contracts the subcontractors that do the work in the field, such as mechanical, electrical, and civil subcontractors, so trade providers show up per the schedule needs, deliver the contracted scope at optimal cost.

The Sourcing Manager works cross-functionally with Construction, Engineering, Finance/AP, Legal, and Operations to lock in subtrade capacity early and minimize commercial and execution risk across capital projects.

Some of the responsibilities you can expect include the following:

* Build a subtrade sourcing plan for each site, including package strategy, target bidders, and a buyout schedule tied to the construction schedule

* Map and prequalify subtrade partners in each market on capacity , safety record (EMR, TRIR, OSHA history), bonding, financial health, manpower, and project history

* Write scope sheets, run competitive bids, and level bids to close scope gaps before award

* Negotiate subcontracts, labor and unit rates, escalation, and manpower commitments, and put program agreements in place with proven partners

* Track trade capacity and competing projects, identifying early risk indicators and escalating before they affect the schedule

* Review change orders, T&M tickets, and claims for merit and price, and keep payments aligned with contractual milestones

* Score subtrade partners after each project and recommend improvements that reduce risk and improve cash flow timing

**ABOUT YOU**

* Bachelor's degree in construction management, Supply Chain, Engineering, or related field preferred (equivalent experience considered)

* 5+ years of experience in subcontract buyout, procurement, or contracts management on large capital projects

* Demonstrated experience leveling trade bids and negotiating subcontracts across multiple trade scopes

* Able to read drawings and specifications

headlined_rolled.desc:

* Own sourcing strategies for specialty construction materials including MV and LV cables, conduit, grounding systems, fiber, , and electrical distribution equipment across the full site supply chain.

* Negotiate supply and frame agreements, including copper and aluminum price adjusters, tariff fluctuation strategies lead time commitments, and warranty terms

* Secure manufacturing slots for long lead equipment and track production against project schedules, identifying early risk indicators such as capacity constraints or sub-supplier delays

* Qualify and dual source critical suppliers so no single manufacturer can stop a project

* Partner with the procure-to-pay team so awarded agreements translate into accurate purchase orders, on time delivery, and payments aligned with contractual milestones

* Report category spend, savings, and supply risk, and recommend improvements that reduce risk and improve cash flow timing

**ABOUT YOU**

* Bachelor's degree in supply chain, Business, Engineering, or related field preferred (equivalent experience considered)

* Demonstrated experience negotiating supply agreements with manufacturers and distributors, including metal price adjustment terms

* Comfortable reading single line diagrams, cable schedules, and e

headlined_rolled.desc:
**Construction Payroll Specialist – Union & Multi-State Payroll**

**Position Summary**

The Construction Payroll Specialist is responsible for the accurate and timely processing of payroll for a construction workforce operating across multiple states and union jurisdictions throughout the United States. This position requires extensive involvement with union payroll, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs), prevailing wage requirements, certified payroll, multi-state taxation, employee deductions, fringe benefits, and job-cost allocation.

The Payroll Specialist works closely with field personnel, project management, accounting, human resources, union representatives, and benefit funds to ensure employees are paid accurately and all payroll-related reporting and compliance requirements are satisfied.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Payroll Processing**

* Process weekly payroll for union and non-union employees across multiple states and jurisdictions.
* Review employee timecards for accuracy, approvals, job numbers, cost codes, work classifications, and applicable pay rates.
* Calculate regular wages, overtime, double time, shift premiums, travel-related compensation, and other applicable earnings.
* Maintain accurate employee payroll records, tax elections, direct deposits, deductions, and other payroll information.
* Research and resolve payroll discrepancies in coordination with employees, supervisors, project managers, and accounting personnel.
* Process payroll adjustments, corrections, voids, and off-cycle payments when necessary.

**Union Payroll & Fringe Benefits**

* Interpret and apply multiple collective bargaining agreements and union wage schedules.
* Maintain union, local, trade, classification, and jurisdiction-specific wage and fringe benefit rates.
* Calculate employer-paid and employee-paid union benefits, which may include health and welfare, pension, annuity, training, vacation, apprenticeship, and other required funds.

**Job description**

Leverage General is a small, trusted commercial general contractor that has been building in the Treasure Valley for four years. We're looking for an estimator to work directly with the owner, run bids from drawings to bid day, and see the results on every job we win.

We build specialty systems, manufacturing upgrades, and tenant improvements, often engineer-driven work with multiple trades. We're also growing our civil, earthwork, and underground utility work, so civil estimating experience is a big plus.

**The role**  
Reporting to the owner, you'll take bids from drawings to bid day. You'll do takeoffs, level sub quotes, run preconstruction with owners and designers, manage buyout, and feed actual job costs back into future bids. We use AI to cut admin work. You check every output and put your stamp on every number.

**How you win here:** typically 5–7 complete, on-time bids a month depending on size and type, at margins that hold up when the job is built.

**Growth path:** as we grow, this seat leads to Chief Estimator or Preconstruction Manager.

**What you bring:** 5+ years of construction estimating, ideally with a commercial GC. Civil estimating is a strong plus.

**The details**

* Remote, work from home, based in the Treasure Valley with regular local job walks and sub meetings
* Competitive market salary, depending on experience
* PTO, health stipend, phone allowance, mileage, equipment and software provided, and a company-performance bonus

We're hiring a Head Bookkeeper to take over our company books from ownership. This is a hands-on role: you'll own the general ledger, reconciliations, month-end close, job costing, and work with our outside CPA firm.

We'll be upfront: you won't start there. * Phase 3 — Re-sync: Work side-by-side with the Coordinator when they return to hand the work back and catch up on anything that changed.
* Phase 4 — Step into Head Bookkeeper: Ownership divides the shared duties between the two roles and trains you on the rest of the Head Bookkeeper work: month-end close, WIP reporting, journal entries, the monthly meeting with our CPA, year-end, and insurance audit schedules. Once the Coordinator duties are fully handed back, your pay moves to $25/hr.
